newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds largely fend off U.S. slide.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds largely fend off U.S. slide.

text.p: *Australian bonds largely fended off Friday's slide in U.S. bonds as the focus centred on Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting amid speculation of a further policy easing.
*U.S. markets are closed Monday for Labor Day.

Australian bonds largely fended off a sharp sell-off in U.S. Treasuries on Friday as the short end got caught up in speculation of a further easing in monetary policy ahead of Tuesday's Reserve Bank board meeting.
Although many economists generally feel that another cut is likely before year-end, most feel it is unlikely that the central bank would move so soon after the last one.

Traders said bill futures were bought up initially in a continuation of Friday's pre-cautionary positioning, taking the September position to high of 92.22 at one stage, indicating a cash rate of 6.78 percent. The position expires on September 12.
Current official interest rates stand at 7.0 percent after July's surprise 50 basis point cut.
Traders said the market will be closely watching the central bank's market operations over the next couple of days for clues as to whether it is planning an easing.

Bond yields were only marginally higher, outperforming the U.S. market, which saw further evidence of an expanding economy with a jump in the Chicago Purchasing Managers Index, making the market even more wary of this Friday's U.S. August non-farm payrolls report.
The U.S. market is closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread dived to its lowest level in over two years, touching 115 basis points at one stage. The U.S. fall also dragged down Canadian and New Zealand debt, with the latter further undermined by political factors ahead of the N.Z. election on October 22.
